The failure is in the frozen driver [`clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py`](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py#L156-L167), which makes this a **finding** (no files edited).

In [`explicit_confirm`](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py#L156-L167), line 161 checks `re.search(r"\bi confirmed\b", t)` instead of `r"\bi confirm\b"` as in the vendored original [`clinicbench/adapters/lab23_dcitl.py.orig`](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/lab23_dcitl.py.orig#L156). Because `"I confirm"` neither matches `\bi confirmed\b` nor starts with `yes|yep|yeah|confirmed`, `explicit_confirm` returns `None`, falling through to `Driver.consent` (where Arm F's `consent_in_code=True` treats a model `"yes"` as `None`) and `Driver.unclear`, which re-asks and hands off on the second unclear reply (`n >= 2`). (`python3 scripts/port_dcitl.py --check` also exits 1 due to this divergence.)
